697aa793cd.q: Why did Francisco Luengo leave his technology consulting career to join Sonora Foods?
697aa793cd.a: In 2008, Francisco's father called him and explained that despite building something good, the business didn't have a real future unless they began manufacturing their own tortillas. His father said: "I trust you and I don't trust anybody else" and told Francisco "you will figure it out." Francisco recognized this as an opportunity to build his own brand with tangible impact on an industry, rather than working for shareholders at a large billion-dollar company.

697aa793cd.rq: If you can trust somebody and they deeply want to work with you and deliver on their promises, that to me is worth more than anything that is on your CV.

36496c6419.q: What are Francisco Luengo's key criteria for recognizing and hiring talented leaders?
36496c6419.a: Francisco looks for three main ingredients in leaders: competitive spirit (people who feel they can achieve and want to achieve), ownership (the attitude 'I can do this and I will deliver'), and commitment. He emphasizes that he gravitates toward people with 'skin in the game' who are deeply committed to succeeding and delivering on their promises, valuing this more than extensive resume experience.

7279389cf4.q: How did Sonora Foods solve the operations manager hiring challenge during COVID?
7279389cf4.a: After three failed hires for senior operations manager roles, Francisco's finance and HR leaders proposed splitting the operations responsibility between themselves instead. The finance person took supply chain while the HR person (with manufacturing background from Club Coffee) took manufacturing operations. They suggested putting half the budgeted salary back into the business and spreading it among the team, which proved successful.

9825ca700d.q: What is Francisco Luengo's problem-solving approach when faced with complex business issues?
9825ca700d.a: Francisco's approach is to distill noise and complexity into building blocks that can be analyzed. He demonstrates this with a pricing problem example, stating: "Is it actually really complex or is this something that is a simple solution?" He tends to think of things as systems and will often identify that what appears complex actually has an elegant foundational solution, like the equation 'billback equals distributor price minus contract price.'

0d63c5ef90.q: How has Francisco Luengo's focus shifted from early career to his role at Sonora Foods?
0d63c5ef90.a: In the 2000s, Francisco's focus was on personal achievement—Frank's compensation, Frank's role, Frank's choices. Over time, his perspective changed to extend his reach and do something for the family, and now his questions center on 'where does a family stand in the next multiple generations?' rather than personal accomplishment.
